facts.fact: A public plaza in downtown New Orleans, set behind the American Italian Cultural Center.
facts.quote: The Piazza d'Italia is an urban public plaza located behind the American Italian Cultural Center at Lafayette and Commerce Streets in downtown New Orleans, Louisiana.

facts.fact: Completed in 1978 to a design by Charles Moore with Perez Architects of New Orleans, and widely praised at first.
facts.quote: Completed in 1978 according to a design by noted postmodern architect Charles Moore and Perez Architects of New Orleans, the Piazza d'Italia debuted to widespread acclaim on the part of artists and architects.

facts.fact: Italian-American community leaders wanted a permanent public commemoration of the Italian immigrant experience in the city.
facts.quote: In the early 1970s, leaders of New Orleans' Italian-American community conceived of a permanent public commemoration of the Italian immigrant experience in the city.

facts.fact: The design is a fountain shaped like the Italian peninsula, ringed by curved colonnades, a clock tower and abstract versions of a campanile and a Roman temple.
facts.quote: In collaboration with Ron Filson of UIG in Los Angeles and two young architects then practicing with the Perez firm in New Orleans, Malcolm Heard and Allen Eskew, Moore conceived of a public fountain in the shape of the Italian peninsula, surrounded by multiple hemicyclical colonnades, a clock tower, and a campanile and Roman temple - the latter two expressed in abstract, minimalist, space frame fashion.

facts.fact: Classical forms and orders are reworked playfully in modern materials such as stainless steel and neon, and with water jets.
facts.quote: The fountain and its surrounding colonnades playfully appropriated classical forms and orders, executing them in modern materials (e.g., stainless steel, neon) or kinetically (e.g., suggesting the acanthus leaves of traditional Corinthian capitals through the use of water jets).

facts.fact: The surrounding development was never built, so the plaza decayed and was sometimes called the first postmodern ruin.
facts.quote: Deemed an architectural masterpiece even prior to its completion, the Piazza in fact began to rapidly deteriorate as the development surrounding it was never realized.

facts.fact: The plaza was fully restored by 2004 alongside the conversion of the neighbouring Lykes Center to a hotel.
facts.quote: The conversion of the adjacent Lykes Center to the Loews Hotel, New Orleans, completed in 2003, was accompanied by the full restoration of the Piazza d'Italia (accomplished by 2004).

facts.fact: A stadium in Sapporo, Hokkaido, used mainly for association football.
facts.quote: The Sapporo Dome (札幌ドーム, Sapporo Dōmu), a.k.a. the Daiwa House Premist Dome (大和ハウス プレミストドーム, Daiwa Hausu Puremisuto Dōmu) for sponsorship reasons, is a stadium located in Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan, and is primarily used for association football.

facts.fact: Opened in 2001 and hosted matches at the 2002 FIFA World Cup.
facts.quote: Sapporo Dome opened in 2001 with 41,580 seats.

facts.fact: It alternates between an artificial-turf baseball field and a grass football pitch that slides in and out.
facts.quote: The Dome switches between two entirely different surfaces: Baseball games are played on an underlying artificial turf field, while association football games are held on a grass pitch that slides into and out of the stadium as needed.

facts.fact: Changing from baseball to football begins with storing the baseball field's artificial turf.
facts.quote: Conversion from baseball to football begins with the storage of the baseball field's artificial turf.

facts.fact: Several stadiums have sliding pitches, but unlike most of them the Sapporo Dome has a fixed roof.
facts.quote: Other stadiums that feature sliding pitches include the GelreDome in the Netherlands, Veltins-Arena in Germany, State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona, United States, and Allegiant Stadium in Paradise, Nevada, United States, along with the split pitch of London's Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and Madrid's Santiago Bernabéu Stadium; however, unlike these facilities (with the exception of Allegiant Stadium), the Sapporo Dome has a fixed roof.

facts.fact: In 2007 it was the first world-championship or Winter Olympic level venue to host indoor, nighttime skiing events.
facts.quote: It also made history as being the first venue where both indoor and nighttime skiing events took place for the first time on a world championship or Winter Olympic Games level with competitions in the cross-country skiing sprints (men's and women's individual, and men's and women's team) and the cross-country portion of the 7.5 km sprint event in the Nordic combined.

facts.fact: For the ski events the turf-conversion hovering system was used to help make the snow.
facts.quote: In order to generate snow, the stadium used its turf conversion hovering system to facilitate the snow making process for the skiing competitions.

facts.fact: A secure backup facility for the world's crop diversity, on Spitsbergen in the Arctic Svalbard archipelago.
facts.quote: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault (Norwegian: Svalbard globale frøhvelv) is a secure backup facility for the Earth's crop diversity on the Norwegian island of Spitsbergen in the remote Arctic Svalbard archipelago.

facts.fact: It stores duplicates of seeds held in gene banks around the world.
facts.quote: The Seed Vault provides long-term storage for duplicates of seeds from around the world, conserved in gene banks.

facts.fact: It officially opened in February 2008.
facts.quote: The Seed Vault officially opened on 26 February 2008, although the first seeds arrived in January 2008.

facts.fact: The vault is cut into a sandstone mountain on Spitsbergen and has robust security systems.
facts.quote: The seed bank is 130 m (430 ft) inside a sandstone mountain on Spitsbergen Island, and employs robust security systems.

facts.fact: An illuminated artwork, Perpetual Repercussion by Dyveke Sanne, runs along the roof and down the front face to mark the vault from a distance.
facts.quote: Running the length of the facility's roof and down the front face to the entryway is an illuminated artwork named Perpetual Repercussion by Norwegian artist Dyveke Sanne that marks the location of the vault from a distance.

facts.fact: The roof and entrance use reflective stainless steel, mirrors and prisms.
facts.quote: The roof and vault entrance are filled with highly reflective stainless steel, mirrors, and prisms.

facts.fact: The design ensured water that seeped in froze after a few metres and the seeds stayed safe.
facts.quote: Warmer temperatures and heavy rainfall in October 2016 caused significantly greater amounts of water to seep into the entrance, but the facility's design ensured that the water froze after several meters and the seeds were not endangered.

facts.fact: Built as the athletes' village for the 1982 Asian Games in New Delhi, designed by Raj Rewal; described as the first of its kind in the Games series.
facts.quote: The site was developed as the athletes' village for the 1982 Asian Games held in New Delhi.

facts.fact: It stands on the remains of the Khalji-dynasty Siri Fort and became a residential colony.
facts.quote: Built on the remains of the 15th Century Khalji Dynasty's Siri Fort over an area of 800 acres (3.2 km2), this residential colony has 853 flats of which 793 house top officials of PSUs, bureaucrats, public servants, and union ministers.

facts.fact: Courtyards are arranged in a hierarchy at different levels of the complex.
facts.quote: The hierarchy of Courtyards is present at different levels of the complex.

facts.fact: Mix of individual houses and low apartment blocks of two to four storeys.
facts.quote: The complex consists of 700 housing units, out of which 200 were individual houses and 500 apartments, which vary from 2 to 4-story structures.

facts.fact: Streets are narrow, shaded and broken into small units, creating pauses and resting points.
facts.quote: Streets are narrow, shaded, broken up into small units, creating pauses, points of rest, and changing points.

facts.fact: Terraces give semi-private space and recall the houses of Jaisalmer.
facts.quote: Terraces that are formed provide semi-private space, which obviously reminds the characteristics of houses of Jaisalmer.

facts.fact: Vehicle and pedestrian movement are separated but closely linked.
facts.quote: Vehicular and pedestrian movement is segregated but closely interlinked for convenience Peripheral roads are connected to cul-de-sac parking areas, which give access to individual garages or car porches attached to houses or apartments.

facts.fact: A mansion in Heliopolis, Cairo, inspired architecturally by Hindu temples; also called Le Palais Hindou.
facts.quote: The Baron Empain Palace (Arabic: قصر البارون إمبان, "Qasr el Baron Emban"), also known as Le Palais Hindou (lit. 'The Hindu Palace'), is a distinctive and historic mansion in Heliopolis, a suburb northeast of central Cairo, Egypt.

facts.fact: Designed by the French architect Alexandre Marcel.
facts.quote: The palace was designed by Alexandre Marcel, a French architect and a member of the French Institute.

facts.fact: Inspired mostly by Angkor Wat and the Hindu temples of Orissa, it was built in reinforced concrete, then a symbol of luxury.
facts.quote: Inspired mostly by Angkor Wat in Cambodia and by the Hindu temples of Orissa in East India, it was built between 1907 and 1911, in reinforced concrete, which was considered a symbol of luxury and status at the time.

facts.fact: Baron Empain came to Egypt to expand his business and build railways, and built the palace as part of founding Heliopolis.
facts.quote: In 1904, Baron Édouard Empain came to Egypt with the intention of expanding his commercial empire and to build railway lines in Egypt.

facts.fact: He hired the architect Ernest Jaspar to help create the 'Heliopolis style' in the new suburb.
facts.quote: By 1906, the Baron hired the architect Ernest Jaspar to help create a unique aesthetic in the suburbs of Heliopolis dubbed the "Heliopolis style." Including aspects of Persian elements to neoclassical European aspects, the newly established city of Heliopolis would become a cultural center of Egypt attracting people from all over the world.

facts.fact: After his death in 1929 and the 1952 revolution the palace was left abandoned.
facts.quote: After the Baron's death in 1929 and the 1952 revolution that took place in Egypt, the palace was left abandoned.

facts.fact: In 2012 an agreement with the Belgian government set out to restore it as an international art and cultural centre.
facts.quote: In 2012, an agreement was signed with the Belgian government to jointly restore the building and turn it into an international art and cultural center.

facts.fact: Built on Buzludzha Peak by the Bulgarian communist government and inaugurated in 1981 to commemorate the 1891 founding events of the socialist movement.
facts.quote: The Monument House of the Bulgarian Communist Party (Bulgarian: Дом паметник на БКП, romanized: Dom pametnik na BKP), also known as the Buzludzha Monument (), was built on Buzludzha Peak in central Bulgaria by the Bulgarian communist government and inaugurated in 1981.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1974 under architect Georgi Stoilov.
facts.quote: Construction of the monument began on 23 January 1974 under architect Georgi Stoilov, a former mayor of Sofia and co-founder of the Union of Architects in Bulgaria.

facts.fact: The mountain peak was levelled with TNT to form a stable foundation.
facts.quote: The peak was leveled into a stable foundation using TNT, reducing the mountain's height from 1,441 metres (4,728 feet) to 1,432 metres (4,698 feet).

facts.fact: It exemplifies the futurist architecture common to many state-built communist buildings.
facts.quote: The monument exemplifies the futurist architecture common to many state-constructed communist buildings.

facts.fact: Mosaics inside commemorate the history of the Bulgarian Communist Party.
facts.quote: Inside the building, mosaics commemorating the history of the Bulgarian Communist Party cover approximately 937 square meters; 35 tons of cobalt glass were used in their manufacture.

facts.fact: A star-shaped red window sat at the top of the hall.
facts.quote: At the top of the monument’s hall, there was a star-shaped red window associated with communism.

facts.fact: Maintenance ended in 1989 and the building is closed because of its weakened structure; the Buzludzha Project is working toward preservation.
facts.quote: All maintenance ended with the fall of communism in 1989, and the building remains closed to the public due to the hazards of the weakened structure.

facts.fact: Europa Nostra named it one of the seven most endangered heritage sites in Europe in 2018.
facts.quote: In 2018, the monument was recognized by Europa Nostra as one of the seven most endangered heritage sites in Europe.

facts.fact: Centraal Beheer is an insurance company in Apeldoorn, Netherlands; this article is about the company, not the building.
facts.quote: Centraal Beheer is an insurance company located in Apeldoorn, Netherlands.

facts.fact: Its offices are known for the architecture of Herman Hertzberger.
facts.quote: Its offices are known for its architecture by Herman Hertzberger.

facts.fact: The main library of the Bartholomew County system in Columbus, Indiana, designed by I. M. Pei & Partners, completed in 1969 and dedicated in 1971.
facts.quote: The Cleo Rogers Memorial Library, also known as the Main Library, is the flagship library of the Bartholomew County Public Library system in Bartholomew County, Indiana, US. It includes a branch in Hope, another branch under construction at the North Christian Church in Columbus, and a bookmobile that serves the county.

facts.fact: It is notable for red brick with concrete details and the Library Plaza, which holds Henry Moore's sculpture Large Arch.
facts.quote: It is notable for its design of red brick with concrete details and its Library Plaza, an urban space punctuated by the sculpture "Large Arch" by Henry Moore.

facts.fact: It was not one of the buildings of the Cummins Foundation Architectural Program, even though Columbus had many such modern buildings.
facts.quote: By the early 1960s a number of modern buildings by young architects had been built in Columbus through the Cummins Foundation Architectural Program, however this building was not one of those projects.

facts.fact: The library, plaza and sculpture relate directly to Eliel Saarinen's First Christian Church and the Irwin House.
facts.quote: The design and placement of the library, plaza, and sculpture directly relate to and recognize the design of First Christian Church (designed by Eliel Saarinen and completed in 1942), and the Irwin House, (designed by Henry Ayling Phillips, and completed in 1910).

facts.fact: A brick pavilion with solid east and west walls and an off-centre main entrance at the west end.
facts.quote: This brick pavilion has solid walls on the east and west and has its main entrance off center at the west end.

facts.fact: Inside, brick, concrete and limestone details continue, and the ceiling is a coffered concrete system with lights set in deep square recesses.
facts.quote: The ceiling is a coffered concrete system with deep inset square elements that contain light fixtures.

facts.fact: Before the plaza, the city had few civic gathering spaces.
facts.quote: Before the Library Plaza was built there were few civic gathering spots in the city.

facts.fact: The plaza uses the same brick and concrete as the library.
facts.quote: The same brick and concrete materials used on the library were used on the plaza.

facts.fact: A residence for graduate students at the University of Toronto, designed by Thom Mayne of Morphosis with Toronto's Teeple Architects.
facts.quote: Graduate House at the University of Toronto is a student residence specifically for graduate students, designed by Thom Mayne of Morphosis Architects in Los Angeles together with Toronto's Teeple Architects.

facts.fact: The new Graduate House opened in 2000.
facts.quote: The new Graduate House opened in 2000 and accommodates 435 students.

facts.fact: It marks the main western entrance to the campus with a long structure extending over Harbord Street.
facts.quote: Located on the western edge of the St. George campus, on the north-east corner of Spadina Avenue and Harbord Street, the residence marks the main western entrance to the campus with a long structure extending halfway over Harbord Street featuring a massive "University of Toronto" sign.

facts.fact: Considered one of architect Thom Mayne's more important works; he won the Pritzker Prize in 2005.
facts.quote: The building is considered one of the more important works of architect Thom Mayne, who won the Pritzker Prize in 2005.

facts.fact: Suites range from two to five bedrooms, with shared amenities such as a reading room and common room.
facts.quote: Graduate House contains two to five bedroom apartment-style suites for full-time Graduate and Second-Entry Professional Faculty single students.

facts.fact: It replaced an earlier residence building, the 1926 St. George Apartments.
facts.quote: Before 2000, the Graduate Student Residence was a building at 321 Bloor St W, known as the St. George Apartments.

facts.fact: A University of Sheffield tower that opened in 1965; English Heritage called it 'the most elegant university tower block in Britain of its period'.
facts.quote: The Arts Tower is a building at 12 Bolsover Street in Sheffield, England, belonging to the University of Sheffield and which opened in 1965.

facts.fact: Designed by Gollins, Melvin, Ward & Partners; construction began in 1961.
facts.quote: Designed by architects Gollins, Melvin, Ward & Partners (GMW), construction of the tower started in 1961 and lasted four years.

facts.fact: No documentary evidence shows it was directly inspired by the Seagram Building; the project architect said the form came from its surroundings.
facts.quote: Contrary to popular belief, there is no documentary evidence to suggest that the design was directly inspired by the similar, but much larger, Seagram Building in New York City, or for the theory linking it to the CIS Tower and New Century House in Manchester, England - although the similarity of aesthetics between the four buildings is undeniable.

facts.fact: Entry was originally over a bridge between fountains across a shallow pool, later drained and covered because wind down-drafts soaked people.
facts.quote: Entry to the building was originally made by a wide 'bridge' between fountains over a shallow pool area in front of the building.

facts.fact: Circulation is by two ordinary lifts and a paternoster, the largest surviving in the UK.
facts.quote: Circulation is through two ordinary lifts and a paternoster lift which, at 38 cars, is the largest of the few surviving in the United Kingdom.

facts.fact: A mezzanine bridge links it to Western Bank Library, by the same architects; the two are meant to be viewed together.
facts.quote: A bridge at the mezzanine level links the tower to Western Bank Library.

facts.fact: Both buildings are Grade II* listed.
facts.quote: The Arts Tower and Library are Grade II* listed buildings.

facts.fact: An urban mosque in Dhaka designed by Marina Tabassum and completed in 2012; it relies on open space and light and shadow instead of domes and minarets.
facts.quote: The Bait Ur Rouf Mosque (Bengali: বায়তুর রউফ জামে মসজিদ, Arabic: الجامع بيت الرؤوف) is a distinctive urban mosque located in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

facts.fact: Sufia Khatun donated land and in 2005 commissioned her granddaughter Marina Tabassum, who then led fundraising, design and building; community donors funded most of it.
facts.quote: In the wake of the tragic loss of two of her daughters, Bangladeshi widow Sufia Khatun donated part of her land for the construction of a mosque.

facts.fact: The site is flood-prone and the building is angled to the Qibla direction.
facts.quote: The building is located in a flood-prone area, and is designed along an axis angled 13 degrees to the Qibla direction.

facts.fact: Rotating the prayer hall to the correct direction created light courts on four sides.
facts.quote: This allowed the designer to rotate the prayer hall to the correct direction and created light courts on four sides with room for other functions.

facts.fact: Random circular openings in ceiling and walls let in light and create shifting patterns of light and shadow.
facts.quote: Dozens of random, circular openings in the ceiling and walls allow natural light to enter the building, creating shifting patterns of light and shadow to enhance the spiritual atmosphere.

facts.fact: Handmade terracotta brick walls provide natural ventilation.
facts.quote: Handmade terracotta brick walls provide natural ventilation, helping keep the building cool even on hot days.

facts.fact: One of six winners of the Aga Khan Award for Architecture in 2016.
facts.quote: The Bait Ur Rouf Mosque was one of six winners of the Aga Khan Award for Architecture in 2016, along with the Friendship Centre in Gaibandha.

facts.fact: A communications tower in Fitzrovia, London, constructed in 1964; originally the Museum Radio Tower.
facts.quote: The BT Tower is a communications tower in Fitzrovia, London, England, constructed in 1964.

facts.fact: Commissioned by the General Post Office to carry microwave aerials for its national telecommunications network.
facts.quote: The tower was commissioned by the General Post Office (GPO).

facts.fact: The taller structure was needed to keep the radio links' line of sight clear of tall buildings then planned in London.
facts.quote: It replaced a shorter, 1940s steel lattice tower on the roof of the Museum Telephone Exchange, so named for its proximity to the British Museum.

facts.fact: Designed by the Ministry of Public Building and Works under chief architects Eric Bedford and G R Yeats; concrete clad in glass.
facts.quote: The tower was designed by the Ministry of Public Building and Works, under chief architects Eric Bedford and G R Yeats.

facts.fact: The glass cladding had to be tinted to prevent overheating.
facts.quote: To prevent overheating, the glass cladding had to be tinted.

facts.fact: Foundations go down through London clay and carry a concrete raft; above sit the aerial section, six floors of suites, a revolving restaurant and a steel lattice tower.
facts.quote: The tower was originally designed to be just 111 metres (364 ft) high; its foundations are sunk down through 53 metres (174 ft) of London clay, and are formed of a concrete raft 27 metres (89 ft) square, 1 metre (3 ft) thick, reinforced with six layers of cables, on top of which sits a reinforced concrete pyramid.

facts.fact: On completion it was the tallest structure in London, until 1980.
facts.quote: Upon completion it was the tallest structure in London and remained so until 1980.

facts.fact: Grade II listed since 2003, which also protects several of its defunct antennae.
facts.quote: The BT Tower was given Grade II listed building status in 2003.

facts.fact: The Madrid headquarters of the Spanish Cultural Heritage Institute was designed in 1967 by Fernando Higueras and Antonio Miró Valverde and built from 1967 to 1970.
facts.quote: IPCE's headquarters is at Calle del Greco 4 in Madrid, Spain.

facts.fact: Commonly called the Crown of Thorns (La Corona de Espinas).
facts.quote: Commonly called "The Crown of Thorns" (La Corona de Espinas), the building was declared a Heritage Site of Cultural Interest (Bien de Interés Cultural) on November 16, 2001.

facts.fact: A four-storey circular reinforced concrete building with a pointed or jagged cornice, one of the most significant examples of contemporary Spanish architecture.
facts.quote: This four-story, circular reinforced concrete building features a pointed or jagged cornice and is one of the most significant examples of contemporary Spanish architecture.

facts.fact: The building houses an institution of the Ministry of Culture dedicated to research, conservation and documentation of Spanish cultural heritage.
facts.quote: The Spanish Cultural Heritage Institute (IPCE) (Spanish: Instituto del Patrimonio Cultural de España) is an institution of the Ministry of Culture dedicated to the research, conservation and documentation of Spanish cultural heritage.

facts.fact: Oslo's municipal public library, described as the country's first and largest.
facts.quote: Oslo Public Library (officially called in Norwegian Deichman bibliotek, Deichman Library) is the municipal public library serving Oslo, Norway, and is the country's first and largest library.

facts.fact: The library itself dates from 1785 following an endowment from Carl Deichman.
facts.quote: The library opened on 12 January 1785 following an endowment from Carl Deichman, who also bequeathed 7,000 books and 150 manuscripts which formed the basis of the library's collection.

facts.fact: The Bjørvika building was designed by the firms Lundhagem and Atelier Oslo.
facts.quote: It was designed by architectural firms Lundhagem and Atelier Oslo Deichman Bjørvika opened to the public on 18 June 2020.

facts.fact: Deichman Bjørvika opened to the public in June 2020.
facts.quote: Deichman Bjørvika opened to the public on 18 June 2020.

facts.fact: It has won several awards, including an IFLA Systematic Public Library of the Year award.
facts.quote: Deichman Bjørvika has won several awards, including the International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions / Systematic Public Library of the Year award.

facts.fact: The building holds manuscripts contributed to the Future Library project.
facts.quote: The building holds manuscripts contributed to Future Library, among them texts by Margaret Atwood and David Mitchell.

facts.fact: Registered users may use the library daily from 7 am to 10 pm, even when it is not staffed.
facts.quote: Registered users may use the library every day, even when it is not staffed, from 7 am to 10 pm.

facts.fact: Jordan's largest airport, south of Amman.
facts.quote: Queen Alia International Airport (IATA: AMM, ICAO: OJAI) (Arabic: مطار الملكة علياء الدولي, romanized: Maṭār al-Malika ʿAlyāʾ ad-Dawaliyy) is an international airport located in Zizya, 30 kilometers (18 miles) south of Amman, the capital and largest city of Jordan.

facts.fact: The original 1983 terminals were demolished in 2013 after new terminals were inaugurated.
facts.quote: The airport's original terminals were built in 1983, and demolished in 2013, following the inauguration of new terminals.

facts.fact: The new terminal design is by Foster + Partners.
facts.quote: QAIA's new design was created by architects Foster + Partners.

facts.fact: The roof was inspired by Bedouin tents and is composed of concrete domes.
facts.quote: The roof was inspired by Bedouin tents and is composed of 127 concrete domes, each weighing up to 600 metric tonnes.

facts.fact: All operations moved to the new terminal in March 2013.
facts.quote: The last flight departed from the old terminal at 10:05 pm on 20 March 2013, upon which all operations were shifted to the new terminal, where its first flight departed at 2:30 am on 21 March 2013.

facts.fact: The airport was originally built to meet traffic growth that Amman Civil Airport could not accommodate.
facts.quote: Queen Alia International Airport (QAIA) was built in 1983 in response to the growing airport traffic needs that Amman Civil Airport could not accommodate.

facts.fact: The official residence and workplace of Pakistan's president, in Islamabad's Red Zone on Constitution Avenue between Parliament House and the Pakistan Secretariat.
facts.quote: The Aiwan-e-Sadr (Urdu: ایوانِ صدر, lit. 'President's Palace') is the official residence and workplace of the president of Pakistan.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1970 and took 11 years.
facts.quote: The construction of the building commenced in 1970, and took 11 years to complete.

facts.fact: Before it, presidents lived in the Prince Palace in Rawalpindi.
facts.quote: Prior to Aiwan-e-Sadr's construction, the presidents of Pakistan lived in the Prince Palace located on the Mall in Rawalpindi.

facts.fact: Built in a modern step-pyramid architectural style, with four main halls named after founding fathers of Pakistan.
facts.quote: The building is built in a modern step pyramid architectural style.

facts.fact: Staff residences, the President's Colony, stand behind the presidency.
facts.quote: Residences for the presidential staff, known as the President's Colony, are also located behind the presidency, adjacent to 4th Avenue.

facts.fact: A concert hall in South Beach, Miami Beach, designed by Frank Gehry, home to the New World Symphony; opened January 2011.
facts.quote: The New World Center is a concert hall in the South Beach section of Miami Beach, Florida, designed by Frank Gehry.

facts.fact: Next to it is a public park by West 8, taken on after Gehry relinquished the job following a budget reduction.
facts.quote: Located one block north of Lincoln Road in the South Beach stretch of Miami Beach, the building also features a new 2.5-acre public park next to it, designed by the firm West 8 (after Gehry relinquished the job following a budget reduction).

facts.fact: Outside visitors can watch free live 'wallcasts' of events on a large projection wall in the SoundScape area of the park.
facts.quote: A half acre of that is the SoundScape area, which allows outside visitors to experience live, free "wallcasts" of select events throughout the season through the use of visual and audio technology on a 7,000-square-foot (650 m2) projection wall.

facts.fact: Acoustics were designed by Yasuhisa Toyota.
facts.quote: The acoustics for the center were designed by Yasuhisa Toyota.

facts.fact: The sky-lit atrium is dominated by Gehry's curved forms and a stack of rehearsal rooms, offices and recording facilities.
facts.quote: However, once inside the atrium, which is lit by the sky during the daytime, the architect's usual assemblage of curved forms dominates, especially in a jumbled stack of over thirty rehearsal rooms, offices, recording facilities, and the like.

facts.fact: Conductor Michael Tilson Thomas described the early design as 'one of Frank's buildings turned inside-out'.
facts.quote: Gradually it started to turn into one of Frank's buildings turned inside-out, which is essentially what it is – and that it was going to be mostly like Miami." Reviews of the New World Center have been favorable.

facts.fact: A museum on the Museumsufer in Frankfurt, housed in an 18th-century building.
facts.quote: The Deutsches Architekturmuseum (English: German Architecture Museum), or DAM, is located on the Museumsufer in Frankfurt, Germany.

facts.fact: Oswald Mathias Ungers redesigned the interior in 1984 as a set of 'elemental Platonic buildings within elemental Platonic buildings'.
facts.quote: Housed in an 18th-century building, the interior has been re-designed by Oswald Mathias Ungers in 1984 as a set of "elemental Platonic buildings within elemental Platonic buildings".

facts.fact: Its permanent exhibition 'From Ancient Huts to Skyscrapers' traces the history of architectural development in Germany.
facts.quote: It houses a permanent exhibition entitled "From Ancient Huts to Skyscrapers" which displays the history of architectural development in Germany.

facts.fact: It runs temporary exhibitions, conferences, symposia and lectures.
facts.quote: The museum organises several temporary exhibitions every year, as well as conferences, symposia and lectures.

facts.fact: Its collection includes architectural drawings and models by Mendelsohn, Mies van der Rohe, Archigram and Gehry.
facts.quote: It has a collection of ca. 180,000 architectural drawings and 600 models, including works by modern and contemporary classics like Erich Mendelsohn, Mies van der Rohe, Archigram and Frank O. Gehry.

facts.fact: An architecturally notable house designed by Sean Godsell as his own family home, built in 1996–1997 in Kew, Victoria.
facts.quote: Kew House is an architecturally notable house designed by Australian architect Sean Godsell as his own family home, built in 1996–1997 and located at 8 Hodgson Street in Kew, Victoria, Australia.

facts.fact: A minimalist glass box encased on two sides by rusted metal screens, cantilevered over a steep slope.
facts.quote: It is a striking minimalist composition, an 18m by 9m glass box, encased on two sides by rusted metal screens, that cantilevers 5.5m over a steep slope at the front of the block.

facts.fact: The 2000 International Architecture Year Book said the house speculates on an Australian vernacular that is a hybrid of east and west, e.g. an open plan with sliding panels and a long kitchen table.
facts.quote: According to the International Architecture Year Book published in 2000, the Kew House "speculates on the emergence of an Australian vernacular born not simply from our colonial history but also from our acceptance of our regional reality as part of Asia.", that is, an architecture which is a hybrid of east and west.

facts.fact: Godsell says the house is 'elemental rather than processed', using rust, oiled second-hand boards and recycled decking.
facts.quote: Although apparently 'modern' in its language, the house is primordial in its intent - rust, oiled second hand boards, recycled decking and a lack of 'precious' detail combine, with rudimentary services to form a house which is elemental rather than processed." The cantilever, which he describes as the 'heroic nature of the structure', is a reference to the post-war optimism of houses in suburbs such as Kew, North Balwyn and Beaumaris.

facts.fact: The Japanese-influenced plan has no corridors; space flows continuously, divided by a central wall and sliding screens.
facts.quote: The Japanese-influenced floor plan has no corridors; the continuous flow of space is divided only by the kitchen/bathroom and a long central wall housing a fireplace and cupboards, and sliding screens between the row of bedrooms and study on the south side.

facts.fact: External screens on the north and west shade the windows from summer sun, and sections can be lifted to let sun warm the interior in winter.
facts.quote: The external screens on the north and west sides shade the windows from direct summer sun, while sections can be lifted to allow sunlight to warm the living spaces on colder days.

facts.fact: The east end is dominated by a built-in table designed as the hub of daily life.
facts.quote: The furniture and artworks were carefully chosen, designed and arranged.

facts.fact: The municipal government centre of Tel Aviv, housing the mayor's office, meeting chambers and council offices.
facts.quote: Tel Aviv City Hall (Hebrew: בית עיריית תל אביב, romanized: Beit Iriyat Tel Aviv) is the municipal government center of Tel Aviv, Israel.

facts.fact: Designed in the 1950s by Menachem Cohen in the Brutalist style.
facts.quote: A new city hall was designed in the 1950s by architect Menachem Cohen, in the Brutalist style.

facts.fact: The large plaza at its foot, now Rabin Square, was designed as a central area for public events and ceremonies.
facts.quote: The large plaza at the foot of the building, first named Kings of Israel Square and renamed to Rabin Square in 1995 following Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin was assassinated at this spot, was designed as a central area for public events and ceremonies.

facts.fact: The municipality was first on Rothschild Boulevard and later used a hotel on Bialik Street as more space was needed.
facts.quote: The Tel Aviv municipality was initially located on Rothschild Boulevard.

facts.fact: The old Skora building became a museum for the history of Tel Aviv in 1972.
facts.quote: In 1972, the old Skora building was converted into a museum for the history of Tel Aviv.

facts.fact: The building is often lit in other countries' flags to show solidarity after disasters and attacks.
facts.quote: The building has been used many times to display solidarity with other countries in times of disasters and terrorist attacks.

facts.fact: The headquarters of the Royal Institute of British Architects, on the corner of Portland Place and Weymouth Street in Marylebone, London.
facts.quote: 66 Portland Place is an office building in Marylebone in Central London, near the boundary with Fitzrovia.

facts.fact: Its design came from a competition announced in 1929 after RIBA outgrew its earlier home; the winning design was by George Grey Wornum.
facts.quote: RIBA had been housed at 9 Conduit Street from 1859.

facts.fact: The competition attracted a high number of entries for a relatively modest building.
facts.quote: The commission attracted 284 entries; a high number compared to the comparative modesty of the construction, but perhaps not surprising given the building's future purpose.

facts.fact: Opened in November 1934 by King George V and Queen Mary.
facts.quote: The building was officially opened on 8 November 1934 by the then King and Queen, George V and Mary.

facts.fact: Designed primarily in Art Deco blended with late neoclassical.
facts.quote: The building is designed primarily in the Art Deco style, blended with late neoclassical (also known as Imperial Neoclassical, after the works of Sir Edwin Lutyens and Sir Herbert Baker).

facts.fact: Its Art Deco elements show in the bronze doors, architectural motifs and a trans-storey main window.
facts.quote: Externally, the Art Deco elements manifest themselves in the bronze doors, architectural motifs, and trans-storey main window.

facts.fact: Listed grade II* in 1970.
facts.quote: On 14 September 1970, thirty-seven years after its construction, the building was listed grade II* (the second highest category in England and Wales).

facts.fact: A listed museum on Museum Island in Berlin, built 1898–1904 to plans by Ernst von Ihne in Baroque Revival style.
facts.quote: The Bode Museum (German: Bode-Museum), formerly called the Emperor Frederick Museum (German: Kaiser-Friedrich-Museum), is a listed building on the Museum Island in the historic centre of Berlin.

facts.fact: It is part of the Museum Island complex, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1999.
facts.quote: As part of the Museum Island complex, the Bode-Museum was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1999 because of its outstanding architecture and testimony to the development of museums as a cultural phenomenon in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

facts.fact: Originally the Kaiser-Friedrich-Museum, it was renamed in 1956 after its first curator, Wilhelm von Bode.
facts.quote: Originally called the Kaiser-Friedrich-Museum after Emperor Frederick III, the museum was renamed in honor of its first curator, Wilhelm von Bode, in 1956.

facts.fact: During World War II part of the collection was stored in a flak tower; fires in 1945 destroyed some collections.
facts.quote: During World War II, portions of the collection were stored in an antiaircraft tower called the Flakturm Friedrichshain for safe keeping.

facts.fact: It was closed for repairs from 1997 and reopened in October 2006 after a major refurbishment.
facts.quote: Closed for repairs since 1997, the museum was reopened on 18 October 2006, after a €156 million refurbishment.

facts.fact: True to Bode's belief in mixing art collections, it now houses sculpture, Byzantine art, and coins and medals.
facts.quote: True to the ethos of its founding director, Wilhelm von Bode, who believed in mixing art collections, it is now the home for a collection of sculptures, Byzantine art, and coins and medals.

facts.fact: A cultural and architectural complex in Valencia, Spain.
facts.quote: The City of Arts and Sciences (Valencian: Ciutat de les Arts i les Ciències, Spanish: Ciudad de las Artes y las Ciencias) is a cultural and architectural complex in the city of Valencia, Spain.

facts.fact: It sits at the southeast end of the former Turia riverbed, drained and rerouted after a flood in 1957 and turned into a sunken park.
facts.quote: The City of Arts and Sciences is situated at the southeast end of the former riverbed of the river Turia, which was drained and rerouted after a catastrophic flood in 1957.

facts.fact: Designed by Santiago Calatrava and Félix Candela, it began construction in 1996 and was inaugurated in 1998.
facts.quote: Designed by Santiago Calatrava and Félix Candela, the project began the first stages of construction in July 1996, and was inaugurated on 16 April 1998 with the opening of L'Hemisfèric.

facts.fact: L'Hemisfèric is meant to resemble a giant eye, an IMAX cinema, planetarium and laserium.
facts.quote: The building is meant to resemble a giant eye, and has an approximate surface of 13,000 m2 (139,931 sq ft).

facts.fact: Its design resembles an eyelid that opens to access the surrounding water pool.
facts.quote: Its design resembles an eyelid that opens to access the surrounding water pool.

facts.fact: The shutter is built of aluminium awnings that fold upward to form a brise-soleil roof.
facts.quote: The shutter is built of elongated aluminum awnings that fold upward collectively to form a brise soleil roof that opens along the curved axis of the eye.

facts.fact: L'Umbracle is an open structure enveloping a landscaped walk with plants indigenous to Valencia, and is the entrance to the complex.
facts.quote: L'Umbracle (2001) – an open structure enveloping a landscaped walk with plant species indigenous to Valencia (such as rockrose, lentisca, rosemary, lavender, honeysuckle, bougainvillea and palm trees).

facts.fact: It was originally budgeted for three structures; added structures contributed to a three-fold cost increase.
facts.quote: Originally budgeted at €300 million in 1991 for three structures, additional structures were added, contributing to a three-fold increase from that initial expected cost.

facts.fact: An art museum in Des Moines, Iowa, established in 1948.
facts.quote: The Des Moines Art Center is an art museum with an extensive collection of paintings, sculpture, modern art and mixed media.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1945, the museum opened in 1948 and wings were added in 1968 and 1985.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1945; the museum itself opened in 1948, with additional wings constructed in 1968 and 1985.

facts.fact: The original wing is by Eliel Saarinen, in a combination of Art Nouveau and Art Deco styles, completed in 1948.
facts.quote: The architecture of the original museum wing was designed in a combination of Art Nouveau and Art Deco styles by Eliel Saarinen in 1945 and completed in 1948.

facts.fact: The second addition, in a Modernist style, was designed by I. M. Pei.
facts.quote: The second addition, originally intended for large-scale sculpture, was designed in a Modernist style by I.M. Pei in 1966 and completed in 1968.

facts.fact: The third wing is by Richard Meier, completed in 1985.
facts.quote: The third wing was designed by Richard Meier and completed in 1985.

facts.fact: Meier's wing was designed to let in as much natural ambient light as possible.
facts.quote: This wing was designed to allow as much natural ambient light in as possible.

facts.fact: In 2009 it also took on operating the Pappajohn Sculpture Park downtown.
facts.quote: In 2009, the Art Center expanded its mission to operate the Pappajohn Sculpture Park, located in Western Gateway Park downtown.

facts.fact: Exhibits product, industrial, graphic, fashion and architectural design in Kensington, London.
facts.quote: The Design Museum in Kensington, London, England, exhibits product, industrial, graphic, fashion, and architectural design.

facts.fact: It began in a converted 1940s banana warehouse on the Thames, altered to resemble an International Modernist building.
facts.quote: The museum was originally housed in a former 1940s banana warehouse on the south bank of the River Thames in the Shad Thames area of London.

facts.fact: It moved in 2016 into the former Commonwealth Institute, a Grade II* listed 1960s building.
facts.quote: In June 2011, Sir Terence Conran donated £17.5 million to enable the museum to move in 2016 from the warehouse to a larger site which formerly housed the Commonwealth Institute in west London.

facts.fact: The conversion was led by a design team under John Pawson.
facts.quote: This landmark from the 1960s, a Grade II* listed building, designed by Robert Matthew/Sir Robert Matthew, Johnson-Marshall and Partners architects that had stood vacant for over a decade, was developed by a design team led by John Pawson.

facts.fact: It opened in Kensington on 24 November 2016.
facts.quote: The Design Museum opened in its Kensington location on 24 November 2016.

facts.fact: A main staircase from the atrium gives access to all floors and views of the hyperbolic paraboloid roof.
facts.quote: A main staircase from the atrium gives access to all floors and offers views to the first and second floors and the hyperbolic paraboloid roof.

facts.fact: The top floor houses a permanent display of key objects from the collection.
facts.quote: The top-floor space under the museum roof houses a permanent display, Designer Maker User, with key objects from the museum's collection.
